ai.summary: Ledgerly sells accounts payable software to mid-size Indian manufacturers and is raising a $2M Seed on a SAFE. The monthly sheet shows ₹48 L revenue in September 2026 (about ₹5.76 Cr a year), growing about 7% a month, with 92 paying customers. The deck's ₹7.5 Cr ARR is 30% above what the sheet supports, so ask how it was calculated before the first call.

traction.reason: The sheet confirms ₹48 L revenue in September 2026 and about 7% monthly growth over six months with 92 paying customers, which is strong for a Seed company. The deck's ₹7.5 Cr ARR is higher than the sheet supports, so this judgement uses the sheet.
evidence: Average growth 7% a month, Apr to Sep 2026 (sheet)

concerns: The deck's ₹7.5 Cr ARR is 30% higher than the ₹5.76 Cr a year the sheet supports

founderQuestions: Your deck shows ARR of ₹7.5 Cr for September 2026, while the monthly sheet shows ₹48 L of revenue that month, about ₹5.76 Cr a year. Could you share how the ₹7.5 Cr was calculated, for example whether it includes signed contracts that aren't live yet?
What valuation cap and discount are you proposing for the SAFE?
Have you raised any money before this round?
Over what period and across how many customers is the 118% net revenue retention measured?
With 11 months of runway, how long will the $2M round last at your hiring plan?

competitors.name: Peakflo
competitors.whatTheyDo: Procure-to-pay and accounts payable automation, with an offer aimed at manufacturers.
competitors.howDifferent: Sells across several Asian markets; Ledgerly is India-only and adds monthly GST credit reconciliation.

competitors.name: Taxilla
competitors.whatTheyDo: Invoice-to-pay automation for India covering accounts payable, GST and vendor payments.
competitors.howDifferent: Comes from GST compliance software, so it overlaps directly on GST; Ledgerly leads with three-way matching for manufacturers.

competitors.name: Mysa
competitors.whatTheyDo: Accounts payable and invoice management software for Indian businesses.
competitors.howDifferent: A general tool for Indian businesses rather than one built for manufacturers' purchase orders and goods receipts.

competitors.name: Procol
competitors.whatTheyDo: Procurement software for Indian companies: sourcing, purchase orders and supplier management.
competitors.howDifferent: Starts at purchasing rather than invoices; it could add invoice matching and move into Ledgerly's space.

competitors.name: Tipalti
competitors.whatTheyDo: Global accounts payable automation suite for multi-country payables.
competitors.howDifferent: Fits the deck's 'global AP automation suites' row, which says they don't reconcile GST and aren't built for India (deck p.7).

marketSize.whatItCounts: Yearly spend if all 48,000 mid-size manufacturers the deck counts paid Ledgerly's own listed prices
steps: Ledgerly's price: ₹25,000 to ₹1.5 lakh a month, so ₹3 lakh to ₹18 lakh a year (deck p.5)
At about ₹85 to the dollar that is roughly $3,500 to $21,000 a year per customer
48,000 × $3,500 ≈ $170M; 48,000 × $21,000 ≈ $1.0B a year, before any share assumption
marketSize.deckClaimComment: The deck's $2.1B uses $44,000 of yearly spend per manufacturer, about twice Ledgerly's top price. Using its own prices gives $170M to $1.0B a year, and Ledgerly would win only a share of that.
